messages:
incident-bot: Paging: HIGH CPU/GPU queue growth detected in cluster 'nebula' (us-west-2). Autoscaler reports repeated scale failures. Impact: inference queue latency rising >5s, some requests throttled. @oncall-anna @sre-miguel please ack :rotating_light:
noncall-anna: Acked. Jumping on it. Looking at metrics now. Queue length reported by router: 12k waiting, 95th p99 latency spiking. Any deploys?
sre-miguel: No deploys from infra in the last 30m. I see a flood of spot preempt events starting ~1769999800, lots of evictions in the nebula GPU pool. Autoscaler tried to spin up nodes but kept hitting GCE quota errors + long boot times.
infra-jess: Confirming GCE quota: GPU quota for project at limit; reserve pool 'reserved-fallback' had only 2 nodes, they were already pinned to other teams. Cloud logs show API 429 on create instances: 
```
Error 429: quotaExceeded: Quota 'GPUs' exceeded for project.
```
No immediate capacity.
eng-scaler: Autoscaler logs show repeated failures: 'failed to create node: timeout waiting for instance to be ready' and then fallback disabled because reserved pool underprovisioned. There's a bug where the fallback policy doesn't consider on-demand fallback when preemptible boot errors >3.
support-lara: Customer impact? Some higher-tier requests are being throttled to keep SLO for others. We have alerting showing a spike in 500s for a small subset of customers using dedicated pools.
pm-omar: From support triage: ~8 customers reported degraded response times, one reported timeouts at 12:02 PT. SLA exposure: some dedicated tenants on nebula-dedicated may breach latency SLA if not recovered in 10-15m.
oncall-anna: Short checklist: 1) move critical routes off nebula to a healthy pool, 2) enable on-demand fallback for critical tenants, 3) escalate quotas with cloud, 4) open oncall bridge if needed. Starting step 1 now.
sre-miguel: Trying to re-route traffic: updating router tag for model routes to point to 'nebula-alt' (same region, verified capacity). Command: 
```
# shift critical model routes
rbctl route update --route-id=prod-models --target-pool=nebula-alt --drain-time=30s
```
Applying now.
infra-jess: Nebula-alt has 60% free capacity but it's on different instance type (A100->A10x4 mixture). Models may have different perf. Watch latency.
eng-scaler: I'm going to temporarily relax the autoscaler policy to allow on-demand fallback: set fallback_policy=on_demand and max_fallback=6. Patch: 
```
kubectl patch cm autoscaler-config -n infra --type merge -p '{"data":{"fallback_policy":"on_demand","max_fallback":"6"}}'
```
Patching. Note: requires node bootstrap; might take 3-6m.
support-lara: Can we mark customers who will be moved? I can update status page: "Limited degradation for subset of customers in us-west-2; mitigation in progress."
pm-omar: Please add note about dedicated tenants, and that we're prioritizing by SLA tier.
oncall-anna: Patch applied. Eng-scaler, any ETA on nodes coming up?
eng-scaler: On-demand nodes requested to cloud. Cloud API accepted 4/6 requests, 2 failed due to quota. Boot logs show container runtime waiting for GPU driver install. I'm pushing a smaller bootstrap image to speed up creation.
sre-miguel: Router confirms partial route shift succeeded: critical routes now 85% on nebula-alt. p95 latency for those routes rose +120ms but steady. Queue for nebula core still large (8k).
incident-bot: Added incident keyword and created bridge link: https://calls.redwood/bridge/1769999999 - oncall-anna joined.
infra-jess: I manually increased reserved pool size by evicting some low-priority jobs (batch training) and freeing 3 GPUs. That freed up partial capacity for fallback. Note: KV cache warm will be cold => extra latency.
eng-scaler: Autoscaler now sees free capacity and started attaching nodes, but saw a repeated preemptible churn. We're switching two requests to on-demand instances to stabilize.
support-lara: Update for customers: "We are routing critical traffic to an alternate GPU pool and provisioning fallback on-demand capacity. Some requests may see slightly higher latency. We're prioritizing customers by SLA." Posting to status now.
pm-omar: Are there any billing/quotas we need to track for on-demand jump? Could bump cost a lot. We should capture cost delta per hour for exec.
oncall-anna: Noted. Finance will want numbers post-incident. For now stabilize.
sre-miguel: Observed root cause hypothesis: A zone-level spot eviction wave combined with an overly conservative fallback threshold in the autoscaler (threshold=0.6 free capacity) meant it didn't trigger early enough. When evictions hit, scale fallback couldn't recover because cloud quota prevented instance creation.
infra-jess: I've filed a quota increase request to cloud console with urgent priority, email to cloud support sent.
eng-scaler: Mitigation checklist status: route shift (done partial), autoscaler fallback set (done), reserved pool increased (done), on-demand nodes requested (partial), quota escalated (in progress). Remaining: monitor for new preemptions and consider cross-region spill to us-west-1 if further instability.
incident-bot: NOTE: customer-facing timer: 00:25 since page.
oncall-anna: Handoff plan: if this is still degraded at +30m, escalate to SRE lead and open customer incident post. For now, @sre-miguel continue monitoring, @eng-scaler keep fallback enabled for 20m and collect autoscaler logs.
sre-miguel: Adding logs snippet of autoscaler error for reference: 
```
E0312 12:05:10.123 autoscaler.go:412] createNode failed: request failed: RPCError(code=ResourceExhausted, msg="Quota exceeded for GPUs in region us-west-2")
```
eng-scaler: Also saw node bootstrap timeouts when image pull retries exceeded 5: 
```
containerd: Pull image for gpu-runtime:5.2 failed: net/http: TLS handshake timeout
```
Potential network flakiness during mass creates.
support-lara: We're tracking 9 total customer reports; 2 are enterprise, already contacted. No escalations to legal.
oncall-anna: 18 minutes in: latency improving on critical routes; overall queue down to ~3k. Continue watch.
pm-omar: Captured action items for postmortem: 1) Lower autoscaler fallback threshold to 0.4 for spot-heavy pools. 2) Add fallback capacity simulation in chaos tests. 3) Improve quota monitoring and preemptive increase. 4) Harden router reroute to account for perf differences.
sre-miguel: Agreed. Also add: autoscaler should try cross-region on-demand fallback if local quotas are exhausted.
eng-scaler: Will add a short-term hotfix: allow autoscaler to split fallback across instance families to improve chance of fulfilling requests during quota pressure. Deploying now.
incident-bot: Metrics: queue length trending down, p95 latency trending to normal. If no regressions, will close incident in 40m.
oncall-anna: Oncall handoff in 40m to SRE lead @sre-miguel if still open. If closed, write post-incident note and notify customers who reported.
support-lara: I'll prepare customer follow-ups and an initial incident message for the support channel.
pm-omar: Thanks team. Keep updates here, flag any customer legal/finance flags ASAP.
eng-scaler: Hotfix deployed. Autoscaler now accepted 4 additional on-demand nodes and split across families. No further preemptions in last 3m.
sre-miguel: Queue now ~600, critical routes stable. Closing bridge in 15m if steady.
incident-bot: Closing note will be posted after 1 hour of stable metrics.
pm-omar: Postmortem owner: @eng-scaler. Please include timeline, impact, customer list, and cost delta.
noncall-anna: Thanks everyone. Moving to monitoring-only. Leaving thread open for 1h. :white_check_mark:
